## Conditional statements

1. Using ifelse, create a new variable for race, race_binary that takes the values "white" and "non-white"

```{r}
dat<-read_csv("https://www.openintro.org/data/csv/acs12.csv")
# recode race into race_binary white/non-white 
dat <- dat |> 
  mutate(race_binary = ifelse(race=="white", "white", "non-white"))
```

2. Using case_when create a new variable for employment that includes an extra level for people who report being employed but have zero income

```{r}
# conditionals with two conditions
dat |> 
  filter(employment=="employed"
         & income==0) |> 
  select(employment, income, emp_recode)

dat <- dat |> 
  mutate(emp_recode = ifelse(employment=="employed"
                             & income==0,
                             "employed but not paid",
                             employment))

dat|> 
  select(employment, income, emp_recode)

# do the same thing with case_when

dat <- dat |> 
  mutate(emp_recode2 = 
           case_when(employment=="employed" & income==0 ~ "employed not paid",
                     employment!="employed" | income > 1000 ~ employed,
                    .default = employment))

```


## Pivoting wide to long

Let's work with a few datasets

```{r}
head(relig_income)
```

1. Use pivot_longer to create a single column for a new variable income from the columns in positions 2 through 11

```{r}
relig_income_long <- relig_income |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = "<$10k" : "Don't know/refused",
               names_to = "income",
               values_to = "count")
```


```{r}
head(billboard)

billboard_long <- billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = "wk1":"wk76",
               names_to = "week",
               values_to= "rank",
               names_prefix = "wk") |> 
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week))

ggplot(billboard_long,
       aes(x = week, 
           y = rank, 
           group = track)) + 
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2)

```

2. Use pivot_longer to create two new columns from the wk columns, one for 'week_num' and one for ranking
